title: Salaries soared, according to annual survey
text:
Salaries soared, according to annual survey

 12/21/00- Updated 10:25 AM ET 

### Salaries soared, according to annual survey

By Ronald Blum, The Associated Press

| | |
| --- | --- |
| | John Mottern, AFP |
| | Outfielder Manny Ramirez signed a $160M deal this offseason, but first basemen averaged the highest salary by position last season. |

NEW YORK — Even before Alex Rodriguez's record payday, baseball players had a boom year at the bank. The average salary soared 17.50% to $1,895,630, according to the annual survey released Wednesday by the Major League Baseball Players Association. The New York Yankees had the highest average salary for the second straight year and the sixth time in seven seasons. A year after becoming the first team to break the $3 million barrier, the Yankees averaged $3,656,542 as they won their third straight World Series title, up from $3,215,660 in 1999.
